items.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: Clifford was always my favorite musician... And we learned that on the ship.

ctx.x: Did you play on a boat?

The only job we had was going over then coming back on the Holland America lines. These were little ships. They’d been on the Indonesian line and they put them in this summer service for the students. These were small ships. We left on June 23, 1956, my 19th birthday that’s why I remember the date, on this little ship, and played ten days over. These were small, slow ships, just students. And you can imagine, it was a ten day house party and we’d play it over, and then we came back the first week in September on…

Clifford Brown was killed. He died on June 26, 1956 on the Pennsylvania Turnpike. Clifford was always my favorite musician, just technique, soul, whatever, just unbelievable. And we learned that on the ship. That was sad. The other thing that happened that summer was the Andrea Doria was sunk. And that’s fifty years ago exactly, 1956. And most people went back and forth to Europe on ships. Plane travel was very tough then. You really had to go up to Gander, Newfoundland and then over to Greenland and then over to…
